2. Heard the learned counsel Sri. V.M Sheelavant appearing for the petitioners; learned AGA Sri Madanmohan M Khannur appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 3 - State and the learned counsel Sri.
K.L. Patil appearing for respondent Nos.4 to 14.
3.

Facts in brief germane are as follows:
The facts of the case dates back to more than a century as is narrated in the petition at hand.
On 1891, it transpires that a lease was executed by one Swamy Rao to the legal guardian concerning CTS Nos.506 to 519; no period of lease was mentioned in the said document of lease.
The grandson of Swamy Rao, later challenges the grant of lease before the Civil Court in C.C.No.232/1965.
The Court holds that it is a permanent lease and not redeemable.

Later, it appears that one NC:
2023:KHC-D:10315 Mahadev Rao executes a deed of management and Will in favour of Ramasa Heerasa Dhongadi.

Based on the deed of management and Will executed by Mahadev Rao and their names have been entered into in the CTS records and compensation is claimed for the acquisition of lands.
4. The matter moves on from that stage on litigation to litigation.

What is germane for consideration of the present lis is that on 03.09.1992 was the name of Ramasa Heerasa Dhongadi was deleted in view of a particular order in CRP No.2056/1976 in respect of CTS Nos.507 to 519.
It is later the names of legal heirs of respondents Nos.4 to 14 submit a representation to the authorities at Hubballi for restoration of the name of the Ramasa Heerasa Dhongadi.
An endorsement comes to be issued that the name that is deleted cannot be restored.
It is then the legal representatives of Ramasa Heerasam Dhongadi approached the Deputy Director of Land Records challenging the endorsement of CTS authorities.
The Deputy Director of Land Records rejects it on the ground of limitation and certain orders passed by the Civil Court.

The legal representatives of Ramasa Heerasam Dhongadi then file a revision before the Joint Director of Land Records in REV No.46/2017-18 and the revision is allowed by condoning the delay and remanding the matter back to the hands of the Deputy Director of Land Records to consider the issue on its merits.
Pursuant to the order of Joint Director of Land Records, the Deputy Director of Land Records dismissed the appeal on the ground that only the Civil Court has got jurisdiction to decide the issue.

The Legal Representatives then file a revision petition before Regional Joint Director of Land Records in RJDLR/REV-6/2021-22 and the Regional Joint Director of Land Records allows the said revision and restores the mutation entries that were deleted way back in the year 1992, i.e., on 03.09.1992.
It is this order that has driven the petitioners to this Court in the subject petition.
6. The Learned Counsel Sri. V.M Sheelavant appearing for the petitioners would contend that the Deputy Director of Land Records initially rejects the petition on the ground of limitation.

The Joint Director of Land Records remits the matter back to the Deputy Director of Land Records, who then hears the matter and rejects the petition on the score that the remedy lies NC: 2023:KHC-D:10315 Shri Shrikant Subbarao Bagalawadi vs The Regional Joint Director Of Land ... on 11 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159380924/
5 before the civil Court.

sentences.text: The Joint Director of Land Records then reverses the order of the Deputy Director of Land Records and restores the mutation entries deleted 30 years ago.
Learned counsel would submit that the Joint Director of Land Records is the same person who had rejected the claim of the respondents sitting as Deputy Director of Land Records.
He would therefore, submit that he has acted as a Judge of his own cause.
7. Learned counsel Sri K.L. Patil would submit on the merit of the matter what has been done by the Joint Director of Land Records is appropriate and does not warrant any interference.
Insofar as the submission that both Deputy Director of Land Records and the Joint Director of Land Records are the same.
He would submit that it is the matter of record, which may require reconsideration at the hands of a different Joint Director of Land Records.

8. Learned Additional Government Advocate would seek to defend the order passed by the Joint Director of Land Records on the score that it is passed by appropriate authority, it was necessity that led to passing the order and he was holding the NC: 2023:KHC-D:10315 post of Regional Joint Director Land Records and therefore, no fault can be found with the that is passed.
9. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and have perused the material available on record.
10. The afore-narrated facts, dates, link in the chain of events are a matter of record.
The only issue that falls for consideration is, tenability of the order passed by the Joint Director of Land Records.
The narration is made in the course of the order.
It would not require any reiteration.
It would suffice if the consideration begins from 2016.
The deletion of the name of Ramasa Heerasam Dhongadi was challenged in the year 2016 before the CTS authorities.
If the story would begin from that stage, it would suffice disposal of the lis.
The authorities rejected the claim of restoration of name of Ramasa Heerasam Dhongadi on 22.02.2016, this was called in question before the Deputy Director of Land Records.
The Deputy Director of Land Records rejects it on the ground of limitation.

The revision was then filed before the Joint Director of land Records, the same was allowed - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10315 by condoning the delay and remitting the matter back to the Deputy Director of Land Records to decide on its merits.
11. It is after the remand, the entire issue in the present lis emerges.
On 25.03.2021 the Deputy Director of Land Records rejects the appeal on the ground of limitation holding that he cannot condone the delay.

The order of the Deputy Director of Land Records, reads as follows:
"10.

The RJDLR who was previously being DDLR and who passed an order of rejection of claim of respondent No.4 to 14 claims to be Lrs of the Ramasa Heerasa Dhongadi vide order Dtd: 25/3/2021 and he was promoted and now officiating as RJDLR Belagavi and thus he ought to have been recused from the case.

The RJDLR is Shri Shrikant Subbarao Bagalawadi vs The Regional Joint Director Of Land ... on 11 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159380924/
6 sitting on his own judgment, as such the Order impugned is illegal, arbitrary and liable to be quashed."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Deputy Director of Land Records (supra) holds that the delay of 25 years in filing the appeal cannot be condoned and therefore rejects the same.
The Deputy Director of Land Records was one Nissar Ahmed.
As could be gathered from the order itself, this fact is not in dispute.

12. An appeal is preferred under Section 136(3) of the Act before the Regional Joint Director of Land Records, who upturns the order and directs restoration of mutation entries that stood deleted in the year 1992.
It is not the veracity of the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10315 order that merits consideration.

But who is the Joint Direct or of Land Records who passes the impugned order, is the same person who acted as Deputy Director of Land Records earlier and had rejected the claim of the very respondents on the ground of limitation.
He now sits in appeal though not directly and passes an order contrary to his own decision when he was Deputy Director of Land Records.
Therefore, he ought not to have sat over as a Revisional Authority as the proceedings before him were hit by 'subject matter bias'.
He ought to have refused himself from considering the petition in which, one of the orders passed was his, which is completely contrary to law as happened now.

13. The submission of the learned Additional Government Advocate that it was doctrine of necessity that led the Joint Director of Land Records to consider the appeal on its merits is sans substance as it would undoubtedly be contrary to the principles of natural justice that once the authority has taken the initial view and those maters spiraling in litigation comes back to the same person later, as revisional / appellate authority in all fairness ought to have recused in deciding the said revision /
appeal, as it would amount to bias.
Bias is of different forms - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10315 and hues.
One such form of bias of the subject matter, apart from pecuniary or personal.

If it is a subject matter bias, as he had already held in the order dated 25.07.2017, the appeal was not maintainable on limitation, he ought not to have sat over the very same proceedings and pass the impugned order dated 28.10.2021, merely because he was promoted and was holding the post of Regional Joint Director of Land Records.

14. Later, on this short ground, the matter requires reconsideration to the present incumbent, the Regional Joint Director of Land Records bearing in mind the observations made in the course of the order.
It is open for the petitioners or the respondents to put forth all the submissions that are presented before the Regional Joint Director of Land Records.
It is made clear that except on the aforesaid issue, the Court has not considered the merit of the matter.
The Regional Joint Director of Land Records presently holding the post shall consider the revision / appeal on its merit and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law.

14. Later, on this short ground, the matter requires reconsideration to the present incumbent, the Regional Joint Director of Land Records bearing in mind the observations made in the course of the order.
It is open for the petitioners or the respondents to put forth all the submissions that are presented before the Regional Joint Director of Land Records.
It is made clear that except on the aforesaid issue, the Court has not considered the merit of the matter.
The Regional Joint Director of Land Records presently holding the post shall consider the revision / appeal on its merit and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law.
For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) The writ petition is partly allowed.
(ii) The order dated 28.10.2021 passed by the Regional Joint Director of Land Records, stands quashed and the matter is remitted back to the hands of the Regional Joint Director of Land Records to consider the issue, bearing in mind the observations made in the course of the order.
